# MCPJam Inspector

- [MCPJam Docs](https://docs.mcpjam.com/index.md): Test, debug, and evaluate MCP servers, MCP apps, and ChatGPT apps across every major AI client.
- [Getting Started](https://docs.mcpjam.com/getting-started.md): Start testing your MCP server in minutes
- [Installation](https://docs.mcpjam.com/installation.md): Here's a list of all ways to start MCPJam
- [Hosted App](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md): Use MCPJam Inspector in the browser, no installation required
- [MCPJam in Claude](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/claude-connector.md): Connect Claude to your MCPJam account through the hosted MCP server: projects, saved servers, evals, and user testing
- [Okta SSO & SCIM](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/sso.md): Install MCPJam from the Okta Integration Network and configure SAML single sign-on and SCIM provisioning
- [IP Allowlisting](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/network.md): The addresses hosted MCPJam connects from, for firewalls and IP allowlists on your MCP and OAuth servers
- [Common MCP Errors](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/common-errors.md): Solutions to common MCP server connection and configuration issues
- [Error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md): What every MCPJam Inspector error code means, the likely causes, and the next step to fix it.
- [Changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overview.md): Track the latest updates, features, and improvements to MCPJam Inspector
- [Home](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/home.md): Org-scoped dashboard with activity stats, recommended servers, and quick-start clients
- [Clients](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/clients.md): Reusable MCP client configurations for testing servers and apps under realistic conditions
- [Multi-server connections](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/connecting-servers.md): Connect to multiple MCP servers with different transport methods
- [Projects](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/projects.md): Group your MCP servers into projects, with the ability to share them with your team
- [MCP protocol versions](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/protocol-versions.md): Pin the inspector to a specific MCP protocol version, including the 2026-07-28 stateless RC, to test how your server behaves across versions.
- [Host Compatibility](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/host-compat.md): See which hosts your MCP server will work in (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot) the moment you connect
- [Skills](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/skills.md): Load and use skills to give your agents the context they need to use MCP tools effectively
- [Playground](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/playground.md): Chat with your MCP servers, invoke tools by hand, render widgets, and inspect every step, all in one IDE-style workspace
- [Evaluate](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/evals.md): Author test cases for your MCP server, run them across models, and gate pass/fail on deterministic assertions plus optional LLM-as-judge.
- [View origins](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/view-origins.md): Which origin your MCP App's view runs at, and how to allowlist it with a third-party API
- [Host presets](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/host-templates.md): What MCPJam's built-in host presets capture, and which fields to get right when you mirror a host in your own Client.
- [OAuth Debugger](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/guided-oauth.md): Debug your MCP server's OAuth implementation at every step of the handshake
- [XAA Debugger](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/xaa-debugger.md): Configure and debug Cross-App Access flows with MCPJam as the test identity provider and client/agent
- [Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md): Test servers that let you connect without signing in and ask for sign-in only when a protected call needs it
- [MCP Inspector](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/tools-prompts-resources.md): Manually test your MCP server's tools, resources, and prompts
- [Tracing & debugging](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/debugging.md): See all messages sent to and from your MCP server
- [Telemetry & privacy](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/telemetry-privacy.md): What the Inspector sends to analytics and error reporting, how links that act as credentials are kept out of it, and how to opt out
- [Launch from Code (Beta)](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/launch-from-code.md): Programmatically launch and configure MCPJam Inspector from your code or build tools
- [MCP Docs Server](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/docs-server.md): Connect AI applications to MCPJam documentation
- [My First MCP App](https://docs.mcpjam.com/guides/first-mcp-app.md): Build a simple Reservation MCP App from scratch
- [My First ChatGPT App](https://docs.mcpjam.com/guides/first-chatgpt-app-react.md): Build a simple Coffee Shop ChatGPT App with React
- [CLI Overview](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/overview.md): Local MCP testing and mcpjam cloud: probing, debugging, OAuth,

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.mcpjam.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Evaluate

> Author test cases for your MCP server, run them across models, and gate pass/fail on deterministic assertions plus optional LLM-as-judge.

A benchmark score doesn't tell you whether your server holds up in production. Evaluate lets you pin down the behaviors you care about (which tools fire, with what arguments, what the final answer looks like) and run them across the models your users actually use.

## Requirements

Evals are available to both signed-in users and guests. Guests authenticate automatically using their guest session, so no sign-in is required to run or generate tests.

## How it's organized

**1. Project**

Holds your servers and your suites. Everything below lives in one project.

**2. Suite**

A group of cases plus the defaults they share: attached servers, models to run against, default assertions, judge config, and argument-matching mode.

**3. Case**

One scenario you want to verify: a prompt (or a sequence of prompts), the tools you expect to fire, an optional expected output, and the assertions that decide pass/fail.

**4. Run**

One execution of a suite. Produces **iterations**: one per case × model. Each iteration has its own transcript, tool calls, tokens, duration, and verdict.

## Authoring a case

Click **New case** in the suite header (or in the empty-state screen when no cases exist yet) to open the case workspace. The case is a draft until you press **Save**: backing out without saving leaves your suite unchanged.

### Case workspace

The case editor is a two-pane workspace. The left column is where you write the case; the right column shows the selected trial: a live run in progress, a persisted iteration from history, or a spec preview.

**Left column: the case spine**

Every case opens in the spine, however it was authored: in the app, through the CLI, or from an SDK suite file. The spine is a flat, ordered list of steps. Each step is one of:

* **Prompt**: a user turn the model receives. The first prompt is always present; use **Add assertion or action** to add a second prompt for multi-turn cases.
* **Interact**: a widget interaction (click, typing) run against a live widget.
* **Assert**: an assertion that grades the case.

Below the step list, an **Expected outcome** field holds the goal sentence the judge grades against.

**Assertions**

Use **Add assertion or action** to add an assertion, a second prompt, or an interact step. Each assertion row says what it checks, who wrote it, and what a miss does:

* **Route**: answers "which tool should handle it?" and carries that answer's strictness: *Reach the tool* allows extra calls, *Exact route* requires the exact order with no extras. The route is always Required.
* **Step N**: an assertion written as a step (what the CLI and the SDK produce). It is graded in place, at its position in the run, and is labelled by that position: a step-level "no tool errors" reads **No tool errors so far**, because it only sees the transcript up to that point. Editing one rewrites that step; it never becomes a case-level assertion.
* **This case**: an assertion you added here. It is graded once, over the finished transcript.
* **Suite**: a default the suite applies to every case. Read-only here, with a link to the suite's **Checks by stage** settings.

The list reads as a checklis/usr/local/bin/npx

# Evaluate

> Author test cases for your MCP server, run them across models, and gate pass/fail on deterministic assertions plus optional LLM-as-judge.

A benchmark score doesn't tell you whether your server holds up in production. Evaluate lets you pin down the behaviors you care about (which tools fire, with what arguments, what the final answer looks like) and run them across the models your users actually use.

## Requirements

Evals are available to both signed-in users and guests. Guests authenticate automatically using their guest session, so no sign-in is required to run or generate tests.

## How it's organized

**1. Project**

Holds your servers and your suites. Everything below lives in one project.

**2. Suite**

A group of cases plus the defaults they share: attached servers, models to run against, default assertions, judge config, and argument-matching mode.

**3. Case**

One scenario you want to verify: a prompt (or a sequence of prompts), the tools you expect to fire, an optional expected output, and the assertions that decide pass/fail.

**4. Run**

One execution of a suite. Produces **iterations**: one per case × model. Each iteration has its own transcript, tool calls, tokens, duration, and verdict.

## Authoring a case

Click **New case** in the suite header (or in the empty-state screen when no cases exist yet) to open the case workspace. The case is a draft until you press **Save**: backing out without saving leaves your suite unchanged.

### Case workspace

The case editor is a two-pane workspace. The left column is where you write the case; the right column shows the selected trial: a live run in progress, a persisted iteration from history, or a spec preview.

**Left column: the case spine**

Every case opens in the spine, however it was authored: in the app, through the CLI, or from an SDK suite file. The spine is a flat, ordered list of steps. Each step is one of:

* **Prompt**: a user turn the model receives. The first prompt is always present; use **Add assertion or action** to add a second prompt for multi-turn cases.
* **Interact**: a widget interaction (click, typing) run against a live widget.
* **Assert**: an assertion that grades the case.

Below the step list, an **Expected outcome** field holds the goal sentence the judge grades against.

**Assertions**

Use **Add assertion or action** to add an assertion, a second prompt, or an interact step. Each assertion row says what it checks, who wrote it, and what a miss does:

* **Route**: answers "which tool should handle it?" and carries that answer's strictness: *Reach the tool* allows extra calls, *Exact route* requires the exact order with no extras. The route is always Required.
* **Step N**: an assertion written as a step (what the CLI and the SDK produce). It is graded in place, at its position in the run, and is labelled by that position: a step-level "no tool errors" reads **No tool errors so far**, because it only sees the transcript up to that point. Editing one rewrites that step; it never becomes a case-level assertion.
* **This case**: an assertion you added here. It is graded once, over the finished transcript.
* **Suite**: a default the suite applies to every case. Read-only here, with a link to the suite's **Checks by stage** settings.

The list reads as a checklis/usr/local/bin/npx

The OAuth suite signs in on its own. When the server needs a sign-in for the other suites too, give them a token, for example from `oauth login --credentials-out`:

| `--mcp-config <path>` | | Explicit MCP JSON config, consulted before `./.mcp.json` and `./.mcpjam/mcp.json`. A missing or invalid file fails setup. |
| `--host <template>` | none | Emulate one host template's handshake and settings. Never launches the real client. |
| `--inference <mode>` | `auto` | `auto`, `byok` or `mcpjam`. |
--

Global `--timeout` bounds each setup operation and MCP request, not the whole run. Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` failed, `2` usage/unsupported/import/policy, `3` credentials, `4` setup/billing/artifact, `5` inconclusive or interrupted; see [Exit codes](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/local-evals.md#exit-codes).

`--host` as a deprecated spelling of `--client`. Passing both `--client` and
`--host` is a usage error rather than a silent precedence rule.

Launch a goal run. **Spends model credits**: fans out into `targets × iterations` chat sessions.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
--
| `--idempotency-key <key>` | No | Replay guard: a retry with the same key returns the run already started and starts no second runner |
| `--expected-sponsored <n>` | No | How many of this launch's conversations you expect to be sponsored (paid from MCPJam's per-user allowance instead of your organization's credits). If the actual split differs, the launch is refused with a `409` and nothing is created. Omit to accept whatever split applies. |

***

--

Each pending request holds one of the account's five concurrent-connection slots for up to an hour. If `connect` reports `ACTIVE_REQUEST_LIMIT`, the error details include the ids of the open requests; cancel the abandoned ones with `connect-cancel` to free slots.

### `cloud projects servers connect-status`

--
| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID |
| `--limit <n>` | No | Revisions per page, 1 to 200 (default 50) |
| `--cursor <cursor>` | No | `nextCursor` from the previous page |

### `cloud projects servers revision`
--

Grade a saved server against a publisher's directory as the platform reaches it, through the saved server row and the authorize exchange. This is the hosted half of `readiness check`: it answers a different question (what the platform sees, not what your machine sees), can optionally run a model for experience observations (included with MCPJam; no credits are consumed), and leaves a persistent record.

All `readiness` hosted commands require an `sk_` API key (via `--api-key` or the `MCPJAM_API_KEY` environment variable) or a prior `mcpjam cloud login`.

--
The `mcpjam` CLI is two invocations. Local MCP testing stays at the top level: inspect, debug, and test MCP servers from the command line or CI (connectivity, OAuth, MCP Apps, tools/resources/prompts, protocol conformance). Most local commands are one-shot; `mcpjam mcp` and `subscriptions listen` keep a process open. Account-bound commands live under `mcpjam cloud` and talk to your MCPJam account. There are no compatibility aliases for the old Cloud paths; see [Migrating to CLI 4.0](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/migration.md).
These stay at the program root. They reject `--api-key` / `--api-url` / `--project`, except `test`, which accepts them only to reach MCPJam-hosted inference.
| [`readiness`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#readiness-hosted-commands) | Grade a server against a publisher's directory. Hosted `start` / `status` / `list` / `cancel` / `report` stay here (leaf `--api-key`; no Cloud project link) | `check`, `start claude`, `start openai`, `start muse`, `status`, `list`, `cancel`, `report` |

| [`cloud eval`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-eval-commands) | Author and run eval suites in your hosted MCPJam projects | `create`, `list`, `run`, `status` |
| [`cloud tunnel`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-tunnel) | Expose a local MCP server through a public MCPJam tunnel URL, registered as a server in your project | `tunnel --server <name> <url>`, `tunnel --server <name> -- <command>` |
| [`cloud clients`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-clients-commands) | Manage clients in your hosted MCPJam projects (`cloud hosts` is a deprecated alias) | `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `servers`, `duplicate`, `delete`, `templates` |
| [`cloud environments`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-environments-commands) | Manage project environments, the host and server bundles eval suites and goals run against | `list`, `get`, `resolve`, `archive`, `ensure-adhoc` |
| [`cloud projects servers`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-projects-servers-commands) | Connect MCP servers to a project and manage pending connection requests | `connect`, `connect-status`, `connect-cancel` |

Usage: mcpjam cloud eval run [options]

Start an eval run of an existing suite, or upload a versioned suite file and run
it. The upload-and-launch has a 120s deadline overall, not per request (raise it
with the global --timeout <ms>); --wait-timeout bounds the RUN instead.

Options:
  --suite <id-or-name>                      Eval suite name or ID
  --file <path>                             Versioned suite file to upload and run (.yaml or .json, or - for stdin)
  --project <id-or-name>                    Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project)
  --server <id-or-name...>                  Override the suite's saved server selection (HTTP servers only)
  --environment <id-or-name...>             Attached project environment(s) to run. Several values start one PAID RUN each.
  --client <id-or-name...>                  Attached client(s) to run, so the run is stamped with that client's config. Several values start one PAID RUN each.
  --host <id-or-name...>                    Deprecated alias for --client. NOT the host-compat catalog id `mcpjam tools --host` takes.
  --all-targets                             Run EVERY attached environment (or, if none, every attached host) — one PAID RUN per target
  --iterations <n>                          Run each case this many times under verdict policy 2 (1-10)
  --repetitions <n>                         Legacy spelling of --iterations
  --case <id-or-title...>                   Run only these cases instead of the whole suite
  --exclude-skills                          Run the 'without skills' arm: no skills are pinned, and the run is labelled as excluded
  --refresh-snapshot                        PERSISTS a new host-config snapshot on the suite, changing every future run of it. Single-target runs only.
  --notes <text>                            Free-text note stored on the run
  --min-pass-rate <n>                       Pass threshold for this run (0-100)
  --match-options <json>                    Tool-call match options for this run, e.g. '{"toolCallOrder":"exact"}'
  --idempotency-key <key>                   Retry key for a lost launch response; for --file, one is minted and printed when omitted
  --wait                                    Wait for every started run to reach a terminal status
  --wait-timeout <ms>                       Maximum time to wait for completion (default 600000; a run held for its judge gets up to 31 more minutes unless this flag is set)
  --reporter <json-summary|junit-xml|html>  Render the completed run report to stdout
  --out <path>                              Atomically write the completed report selected by --reporter (default: json-summary)
  --compose-client <id-or-name>             Compose a stack to run instead of naming a saved environment: the client it runs as. Default is EPHEMERAL (does not attach to the suite).
  --compose-host <id-or-name>               Deprecated alias for --compose-client

The eval run is blocked, and I can't resume it yet. The environment hasn't said the account issue is resolved.

**Blocker:** Launching the suite `suite_fixture` ("Arithmetic smoke") against `server_fixture` was refused with `FORBIDDEN`, reason `PLATFORM_FEE_REQUIRED`. The message says the work needs platform credits. It is separate from iteration and model-step limits. It also says the response doesn't establish the balance or the expected cost.

**What I found:**
- **Credentials:** The CLI authenticates with the API key as `[EMAIL REDACTED]` on the team plan. It sees `org_fixture` ("Fixture organization", team plan, role owner).
- **Project and suite:** `project_fixture` contains one suite and one saved server, "Arithmetic". The saved server is addressed by its ID, `server_fixture`. I couldn't pass the URL `http://fixture:8765/mcp` directly, because `--server` only accepts saved servers.
- **Usage, credits and cost:** I couldn't get a balance, usage figure or cost estimate. The fixture API returned 404 for `/usage`, `/credits`, `/billing` and `/cost`. The CLI's `cloud` commands have no billing or credits command. They cover orgs, projects, sessions, eval, tunnel, clients and environments.
- **Cost in the docs:** The docs say launching a run "spends model credits". A run fans out into targets × iterations chat sessions. Part of the cost may come from MCPJam's per-user allowance instead of org credits. `--expected-sponsored <n>` is documented on goal-run launches. I didn't check whether `eval run` accepts it.

**Next action for this account:** As the owner, review the balance and top-up options under Organizations > Billing for `org_fixture`. Top-ups may require a plan upgrade. I haven't bought anything or contacted production billing.

**To resume once the account issue is resolved:**
```
npx -y @mcpjam/cli@latest cloud eval run --project project_fixture --suite suite_fixture \
  --server server_fixture --idempotency-key trial-1 --wait \
  --reporter json-summary --out /workspace/report.json
```
Exit code 3 (credentials) is the CLI's code for the failure above. Exit code 4 would mean a setup or billing problem.

**Concern note:**
- **Expected:** a discoverable balance and cost estimate, then a run.
- **Observed:** no usage or cost route, and the run was refused for platform credits.
- **Missing:** the credit balance and the expected cost of one iteration.
- **Next:** when the environment reports the issue fixed, rerun the command above. Nothing has been saved to `report.json` yet.
